proposed_widenings.name: unknown_spell_cast_attempt
proposed_widenings.justification: The item's core procedure is not a fixed granted spell. It lets the wielder choose any qualifying Wizard spell they do not know, spend a spell slot of that spell's level, make an Arcana check, and only on success actually cast that chosen spell using its normal casting time.
proposed_widenings.evidence: "While holding the hat, you can try to cast a level 1+ spell you don't know... Once you decide on the spell, you must expend a spell slot of the spell's level. Then, to determine whether you cast the spell, make an Intelligence (Arcana) check... On a successful check, you cast the spell using its normal casting time"

proposed_widenings.name: conditional_success_reset_resource
proposed_widenings.justification: The current activated-ability header consumes its resource at activation time. Hat of Many Spells instead spends the spell slot before the check, but the short-rest lockout starts only on a successful check. That needs success-gated resource consumption/reset semantics.
proposed_widenings.evidence: "Once you decide on the spell, you must expend a spell slot of the spell's level... On a successful check, you cast the spell... and you can't use this property again until you finish a Short or Long Rest."

proposed_widenings.name: effect_atom_create_companion_from_catalog
proposed_widenings.justification: Several failure branches summon creatures chosen from a random table, with control and dismissal parameters, from inside a random-table outcome. The surface currently has spawned-creature as a top-level mechanics family, not as a branchable effect atom inside activation phases.
proposed_widenings.evidence: "A creature appears in an unoccupied space as close to you as possible... it disappears after 1 hour or when it drops to 0 Hit Points. Roll 1d4 to determine the creature" and "A Hostile Swarm of Bats flies out of the hat"

proposed_widenings.name: effect_atom_create_object_or_temporary_magic_item
proposed_widenings.justification: Failure branches create concrete nonmagical objects and a temporary magic item from random tables. The current surface has no object-creation effect atom in types.ts, and no way to express temporary created-item disappearance inside this item's random table.
proposed_widenings.evidence: "You pull a nonmagical object out of the hat" and "You pull a magic item out of the hat... The GM chooses the item, which disappears after 1 hour if it's not consumed or destroyed before then."

notes: No content file was authored. The core procedure cannot be represented honestly with current magic-item activation semantics. Secondary text such as Spellcasting Focus is also outside the current authored mechanics surface, but it is not the main blocker.
